articles.title: Complainant in POCSO FIR against Avimukteshwaranand does a U-turn: ‘Was pressured into filing a fake case’ | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Ashutosh Brahmachari, a disciple of Swami Rambhadracharya, has alleged that he was pressured into filing a false case against Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati and his associates.  Brahmachari claims the conspiracy involved Mahant Ramchandra Das, who lives in Chitrakoot ashram, and several officials. He alleges Das may have even planned to kill Rambhadracharya. The Prayagraj police registered a case of sexual assault on minors against the accused under POCSO provisions.  Avimukteshwaranand and Das, both from Pratapgarh district, secured anticipatory bail in the case.

articles.title: Man gets 20 years’ jail for sexual assault of minor girl in Villupuram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 36-year-old man, P. Siva, was sentenced to 20 years in prison and fined ₹10,000 by a special court for the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in Villupuram, India.  Siva was convicted of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old girl who had lost both parents and was staying at a relative's house. The Tindivanam All Women Police registered a case and arrested Siva on October 10, 2020. The court also ordered ₹5 lakh in compensation for the survivor.

The special court ordered police to lodge an FIR under the POCSO Act, while the Allahabad High Court granted anticipatory bail to Saraswati and others.

articles.title: Why has Belfast erupted in anti-immigrant violence after a knife attack? | Migration News | Al Jazeera

The incident has fueled tensions surrounding immigration policies and sparked calls for increased security measures from politicians like Gavin Robinson and Nigel Farage. The court also recommended exploring a separate legal framework for children born from such pregnancies.

The ED alleges that these individuals conspired and laundered funds through Young Indian, a company they controlled, allegedly acquiring properties worth ₹2,000 crore from Associated Journals Limited (AJL), publisher of the National Herald newspaper.  The trial court's order stated that the agency's probe stemmed from a private complaint and not an FIR, arguing that cognisance cannot be taken on such complaints. The ED argues that this decision is flawed and undermines its efforts to prosecute money laundering cases.

articles.title: ED searches house of Kolkata Deputy Police Commissioner, arrests businessman; Mamata hits back - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: ED conducted searches at the residence of Kolkata Police Deputy Commissioner Shantanu Sinha Biswas and a businessman's premises in connection with a money laundering case.  The agency recovered over ₹1 crore cash and a large quantity of gold from the businessman's house, who was subsequently arrested. Mamata Banerjee, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, accused the ED of politically motivated actions, while Suvendu Adhikari, the Leader of Opposition in the State Assembly, supported the searches as targeting "thieves." The searches follow raids on Trinamool candidates' homes and offices by the Income Tax Department earlier this week.  The West Bengal assembly elections are scheduled for April 23 and 29.

The boycott was prompted by anger over the alleged failure of the BJP to prevent "proxy war" by armed groups against indigenous people, with Meitei women's groups and civil society organizations calling for a five-day shutdown. The United Naga Council (UNC) joined the Meitei groups in extending the shutdown to seven days following the killing of two Tangkhul Naga men allegedly by Kuki extremists.

The incident is under investigation by both the police and state authorities.

articles.title: Justice is served in Sattankulam - The Hindu

The case serves as a precedent for holding law enforcement accountable for delayed fatal consequences of torture.

articles.title: Justice denied: why families of apartheid victims are still searching for answers | South Africa | The Guardian
